samples.summary: Format painter falls back to reading the run *before* the selection when the selection's end block is not a top-level context block (e.g. a drag from the end of a paragraph into a table)
samples.evidence: `formatSourcePosition()` handles `normalized.start.offset >= startLen` by walking `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` from `startIdx+1` to `endIdx`. `getContextBlocks()` returns only top-level body/header/footer blocks — a selection whose `end.blockId` is a block inside a table cell yields `endIdx === -1`, so the guard `endIdx >= startIdx` is false, the loop is skipped, and the function returns `{ blockId: normalized.start.blockId, offset: normalized.start.offset }`. Because `caretInlineStyle` resolves an offset equal to the block length to the block's *last* run, this copies the format of the run immediately preceding the selection — precisely the failure the `+1` and the forward walk were added to prevent (see the docstring at lines 405-410). The same happens when `startIdx === -1` (selection starting inside a table cell but not as a cell rectangle). Result: the painter silently picks up the wrong format for these drags.

samples.summary: Page Setup dialog's room check (`>= pageWidth`) is weaker than `assertUsablePageSetup`'s (`> width - MIN_CONTENT_PX`) for non-integer paper dimensions, so Apply can throw an uncaught RangeError
samples.evidence: The dialog enables Apply when `parsed.left + parsed.right < pageWidth`; `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:987) throws when `margins.left + margins.right > width - MIN_CONTENT_PX` (i.e. > width - 1). For integer page widths the two agree, but `paperSize` can be non-integer — a document whose page size arrived from a collaborator's CRDT write (`resolvePageSetup` only requires finite and > 0, it does not round). With e.g. width 815.5 and margins summing to 815 the dialog considers the setup valid and `handleSubmit` calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)`, which throws a RangeError out of the React submit handler with no try/catch anywhere on the path (`handleSubmit` -> `setPageSetup` -> `writePageSetup` -> `assertUsablePageSetup`).

samples.summary: `getStore().setPageSetup()` writes the store but leaves the editor's cached `Doc._document` and layout stale; the next ruler drag reads the stale value and overwrites the store write
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` calls `docStore.setPageSetup(resolvePageSetup(setup))` and deliberately skips `doc.refresh()` / `invalidateLayout()` / `render()`. `Doc` caches the document (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:99,108,123`), so after this call `EditorAPI.getPageSetup()` (editor.ts:3061, which reads `doc.document.pageSetup`) still returns the *old* geometry and the canvas keeps the old margins. Worse, `ruler.onMarginChange` (editor.ts:2094) rebuilds the setup from the same stale `doc.document.pageSetup` and writes it back through `writePageSetup`, silently discarding the store-level page-setup write. The wrapper newly validates and resolves this path, which makes it look supported, but the read side was never wired up.

samples.summary: `parsePageSetup` still double-swaps landscape geometry, and the new `resolvePageSetup` clamp now measures margins against the wrong axis for such documents
samples.evidence: Word stores a landscape section with `w:pgSz w:w` already the *long* edge plus `w:orient="landscape"`. `parsePageSetup` assigns that long edge to `paperSize.width` and also sets `orientation = 'landscape'`, so `getEffectiveDimensions` swaps a second time and reports a portrait box. The new `resolvePageSetup(...)` call added on this line inherits that: `fitMargins` is now applied with `width = paperSize.height` and `height = paperSize.width`, so an imported landscape document's margins are clamped against the transposed axes. The pre-existing swap bug is out of diff, but routing the parse result through the resolver makes it affect the stored margins, not just the effective dimensions. No landscape case is covered by `packages/docs/test/import/docx-parser.test.ts`.

samples.summary: `getPageSetup()` is called unguarded from an effect, contradicting the toolbar comment that claims only the painter reaches a new `EditorAPI` member at mount
samples.evidence: docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:97-131 justifies `supportsPainter()` by asserting that `getPageSetup`/`setPageSetup` are reached only "behind an `open` guard ... where a missing method costs one press". In fact `DocsPageSetupDialog`'s `useEffect` (`if (!open || !editor) return; const current = editor.getPageSetup();`) runs inside an effect, so an editor lacking `getPageSetup` throws during commit and takes the tree down exactly like the mount case the painter guard exists to prevent — the guard is applied to the less exposed of the two.

samples.summary: `fitMargins` can clamp a legitimate-but-large margin pair down to a 1 px content box, which downstream pagination turns into a per-character line count
samples.evidence: `MIN_CONTENT_PX = 1` means `fitMargins` will scale margins so that exactly 1 px of content width remains (e.g. Letter 816 px with 5000 px margins -> left+right = 815). `PdfExporter` then computes `contentWidth = 1` (pdf-exporter.ts:98) and feeds it to `computeLayout`/`paginateLayout`, producing roughly one character per line and one line per page — an export that appears to hang or exhausts memory rather than failing. The prior raw read produced a negative content width, so this is not strictly a regression, but the clamp chooses a value that is usable in principle and unusable in practice.
